extracted.intended_audience: writers entering short story competitions / aspiring short story writers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting short stories to writing competitions, focusing on how judges typically evaluate entries and how writers can tailor their work to meet those expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Cohesion
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-structured story should have a clear beginning, middle, and end, with smooth transitions between scenes and events. Pay attention to the pacing of your story, ensuring that it flows naturally and keeps readers engaged from start to finish. Clarity in writing is crucial; avoid ambiguity and convoluted language, opting instead for clear and concise prose that effectively conveys your ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure logical scene-to-scene transitions and a discernible narrative arc. Monitor pacing so the story neither rushes nor stalls. Avoid ambiguous phrasing or unnecessarily complex sentences that obscure meaning. Anti-patterns: fragmented or disjointed structure, jarring scene breaks, and convoluted wording that confuses readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and Creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges look for original and creative storytelling that sets entries apart from the competition. Avoid clichés and tired tropes, opting instead for fresh and innovative narratives that surprise and delight readers. Consider experimenting with unconventional narrative structures or perspectives to add depth and complexity to your story. Embrace your unique voice and don't be afraid to take risks and push the boundaries of traditional storytelling conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for surprising choices in plot, perspective, or structure while maintaining coherence. Use voice and image to distinguish your story. Anti-patterns: relying on familiar tropes without a new angle, predictable plots, or safe, derivative writing. Examples of creative moves: unusual point-of-view, nonlinear timelines, subversive twist on a trope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development and Depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Compelling characters are at the heart of any memorable short story; judges pay close attention to the development and depth of the characters portrayed. Create well-rounded characters with distinct personalities, motivations, and arcs that resonate with readers. Show, rather than tell, their traits and emotions through dialogue, actions, and interactions with other characters. Explore the complexities of human nature, delving into the internal conflicts and dilemmas that drive your characters' decisions and behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build characters who change or reveal layers over the course of the story; give them clear wants and motivations. Use concrete actions and dialogue to demonstrate character rather than exposition. Anti-patterns: flat or stereotypical characters, heavy-handed exposition about feelings, or characters who serve only as plot devices without inner life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Theme and Prompt
rubrics_metrics.description: When a competition provides a theme or prompt, judges assess entries based on how effectively they adhere to and interpret it. Ensure that your story not only incorporates the thematic elements but also explores them in-depth, offering unique insights and perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate the theme organically so it enhances the narrative rather than feeling tacked on. Avoid forced or contrived references to the theme; token mentions that don't deepen the story are penalized. Strong entries will illuminate the theme through character, action, and image rather than blunt explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polish, Editing, and Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Polish your work to perfection, seeking feedback from peers or mentors to refine your storytelling skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise for grammar, clarity, and tightness of prose; proofread for typos and formatting issues before submission. Solicit feedback and incorporate constructive criticism. While the page doesn't list explicit formatting rules, presentation often affects judges' impressions—submit a clean, professional manuscript and adhere to any stated contest requirements. Anti-patterns: submitting unpolished drafts, ignoring feedback, or failing to clean up mechanical errors.
